¹ In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah. ² He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. Why stir up trouble that will only bring you down — and Judah with you?"

¹¹ But Amaziah refused to listen. ¹ In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel, and he reigned for nine years. ² He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, though not as the kings of Israel before him had been. ³ Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute. ⁴ But the king of Assyria uncovered a conspiracy by Hoshea: he had sent envoys to So king of Egypt, and he had stopped paying the yearly tribute to the king of Assyria. They had worshiped other gods ⁸ and followed the practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before them, as well as the customs introduced by the kings of Israel. ⁹ The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. They built for themselves high places in all their towns, from the watchtowers to the fortified cities. ¹⁰ They set up sacred stones and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

¹¹ At every high place they burned incense, as the nations the LORD had driven out before them had done. Observe my commandments and decrees, in accordance with all the Law I commanded your ancestors and delivered to you through my servants the prophets." ¹⁴ But they would not listen. They were as stubborn as their ancestors, who had refused to trust in the LORD their God. ¹⁵ They rejected his decrees and the covenant he had made with their ancestors, and they ignored the warnings he had given them. They chased worthless idols and became worthless themselves, following the nations around them — though the LORD had commanded them not to do as those nations did.

¹⁶ They abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God. They made two idols cast in the shape of calves, and they made an Asherah pole; they bowed down to all the starry hosts and worshiped Baal. ¹⁷ They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire; they practiced divination and sought omens. They sold themselves to do evil in the LORD's eyes, and so provoked his anger. ¹⁸ The LORD was furious with Israel and removed them from his presence. Only the tribe of Judah remained. ¹⁹ Even Judah did not keep the commands of the LORD their God — they followed the practices that Israel had introduced. ²⁰ So the LORD rejected all the people of Israel; he afflicted them and handed them over to plunderers, until at last he cast them from his presence.

²¹ When he had torn Israel away from the house of David, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat their king. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns. ²⁵ When they first settled there, they did not honor the LORD — so the LORD sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of them.

²⁶ Word was sent to the king of Assyria: "The peoples you deported and settled in the towns of Samaria don't know the requirements of the god of that land. Let him go and live there and teach the people what the god of the land requires." ²⁸ So one of the priests who had been exiled from Samaria came back and settled in Bethel, teaching the people how to honor the LORD. ²⁹ But each national group kept making its own gods in the towns where they had settled, and they placed these gods in the shrines the Samaritans had made, each group in the town where they lived. ³⁰ The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth; the men of Cuth made Nergal; the men of Hamath made Ashima;

³¹ the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim. ³² They worshiped the LORD, but they also appointed all sorts of their own people as priests of the high places, who offered sacrifices for them in the shrines. ³³ They worshiped the LORD, but they also served their own gods, following the customs of the nations from which they had been brought. ³⁴ To this day they persist in their old practices. They do not truly worship the LORD, nor do they follow the decrees and ordinances, the laws and commands that the LORD gave to the descendants of Jacob, whom he named Israel. ³⁵ The LORD had made a covenant with them and commanded them: "Do not worship other gods or bow down to them or serve them or sacrifice to them.

³⁶ It is the LORD who brought you out of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm — him you shall worship, him you shall bow down to, and to him you shall offer sacrifice. ³⁷ And the decrees, the ordinances, the laws, and the commands he wrote for you — you shall always be careful to obey. You must not worship other gods. ³⁸ Do not forget the covenant I made with you, and do not worship other gods. ³⁹ Rather, worship the LORD your God; it is he who will deliver you from all your enemies." ⁴⁰ But they refused to listen. They kept on doing as they had done before.
⁴¹ And so these nations worshiped the LORD, but they also served their carved images. Their children and grandchildren continued doing as their fathers had done — and they do to this day.

¹ In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah became king. ² He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. There was no one like him among all the kings of Judah, either before him or after him.

⁶ He held fast to the LORD and never stopped following him; he kept the commands the LORD had given to Moses. ⁷ The LORD was with him, and he succeeded in everything he attempted. It was in the sixth year of Hezekiah — that is, the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel — that Samaria fell.

¹¹ The king of Assyria deported Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, along the Habor River in Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes. ¹² This happened because they had not obeyed the LORD their God — they had violated his covenant and disregarded all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded; they neither listened nor obeyed. ¹³ In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them. ¹⁴ Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish: "I have done wrong. Withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand." The king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah a payment of three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold. ¹⁵ Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the LORD's temple and in the treasuries of the royal palace.

¹⁶ At that time Hezekiah stripped the gold from the doors of the LORD's temple and from the doorposts he himself had overlaid with gold, and he gave it all to the king of Assyria. ¹⁷ The king of Assyria sent his supreme commander, his chief officer, and his field commander from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a large army to Jerusalem. Who do you think you're relying on to rebel against me?'"

²¹ "Look — you're trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff. If anyone leans on it, it pierces his hand and goes right through. You're counting on Egypt for chariots and cavalry — how is that going to work? ²⁵ And do you think I've come to attack this place without the LORD's approval? The LORD himself told me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"

²⁶ Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to the field commander, "Please speak to us in Aramaic — we understand it. ³¹ "Don't listen to Hezekiah! This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me, surrender to me, and every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree and drink water from his own cistern — ³² until I come to take you to a land just like your own, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey. Choose life and not death! Don't listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you by saying, 'The LORD will deliver us.' ³³ Has the god of any other nation ever rescued his land from the power of the king of Assyria? ³⁴ Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Did they deliver Samaria from my power? ³⁵ Who among all the gods of these lands has saved his country from my hand? Why then should the LORD rescue Jerusalem from my hand?"

³⁶ But the people kept silent and said nothing in reply — because the king had commanded, "Don't answer him." ³⁷ Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported to him what the field commander had said.

⁶ Isaiah replied to them, "Tell your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of what you have heard — those words with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me. ⁷ I am going to put a spirit in him so that when he hears a certain report, he will return to his own country, and there I will have him cut down by the sword.'" ⁸ So the field commander withdrew, and when he found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, he learned that the king had left Lachish. ⁹ Then Sennacherib received word that Tirhakah king of Cush had set out to fight against him. So he sent messengers to Hezekiah again with this message: ¹⁰ "Say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let the god you trust in deceive you when he says, 'Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.'"

¹¹ "You yourself have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the countries — they destroyed them completely. Where is the king of Arpad? Where is the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, or of Ivah?" ¹⁴ Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the LORD's temple and spread it out before the LORD. ¹⁵ Hezekiah prayed to the LORD: "LORD, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. ¹⁶ "LORD, bend down your ear and listen. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. So of course they could be destroyed. ¹⁹ But now, LORD our God, please deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone, LORD, are God." ²⁰ Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I have heard your prayer concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria."
